taxa.description: Soft-bodied marine gastropods; huge diversity on tropical reefs and temperate walls.
taxa.id_tips: Look for bright colors, rhinophores on the head, and gill tufts on the back. Often on sponges or hydroid.

taxa.description: Intelligent cephalopods; day or night depending on species.
taxa.id_tips: Eight arms, soft sack-like body, often under ledges or in bottles/cans on muck sites.

taxa.description: Elongated predatory fish often hanging mid-water near reefs and wrecks.
taxa.id_tips: Silver body, pointed snout, visible teeth; often solitary or in schools.

taxa.description: Large reef predators; many species site-attached under ledges.
taxa.id_tips: Heavy body, large mouth, often under overhangs. Pattern and size separate species.

taxa.description: Snake-like reef eels living in holes and crevices; constantly opening mouth to breathe.
taxa.id_tips: Look into holes and under ledges for a patterned head and continuous dorsal fin.
taxa.danger_notes: Bite if provoked; do not feed or put hands in holes.

taxa.description: Venomous scorpaenid with fan-like fins; invasive in the Atlantic/Caribbean.
taxa.id_tips: Bold striping, elaborate pectoral fins, hovering near structure.

taxa.description: Flattened cartilaginous fishes; many rest on sand or cruise along walls.
taxa.id_tips: Diamond/disc body, long tail; check sand patches and blue water for pelagic species.
taxa.danger_notes: Some stingrays have barbs — shuffle feet in shallow sand.

taxa.description: Giant filter-feeding rays; often at cleaning stations or plankton blooms.
taxa.id_tips: Cephalic fins (horns), no stinging barb, huge wingspan, mouth at front.

taxa.description: Elegant spotted rays that fly over sand and reef in pairs or schools.
taxa.id_tips: White spots on dark dorsal surface, pointed snout, long whip tail.

taxa.description: Reef-building and soft anthozoans that structure dive sites.
taxa.id_tips: Hard corals have stony skeletons; soft corals and gorgonians sway. Brain coral has maze-like valleys.

taxa.description: Large crustaceans under ledges and in wrecks; antennae often stick out first.
taxa.id_tips: Look under overhangs for antennae and armored carapace.

taxa.description: Air-breathing reptiles commonly seen grazing or resting on reefs.
taxa.id_tips: Shell shape and beak distinguish green vs hawksbill; don't chase or ride.

taxa.description: Critically endangered reef turtle with overlapping scutes and a hawk-like beak.
taxa.id_tips: Pointed beak, serrated rear shell edge, overlapping scutes.

taxa.description: Large herbivorous turtle often on seagrass and shallow reefs.
taxa.id_tips: Rounded head, smooth non-overlapping scutes, often grazing.

taxa.description: Camouflaged ambush predators; stonefish are among the most venomous fishes.
taxa.id_tips: Scan sand and rubble for eyes and fin outlines that don't match the substrate.
taxa.danger_notes: Venomous dorsal spines — careful hand/knee placement.

taxa.description: Diverse crustaceans on reef, muck, and night dives.
taxa.id_tips: Check crevices and anemones at night; hermit crabs carry shells.

taxa.description: Generic PADI/label bucket for mixed tropical reef assemblage.
taxa.id_tips: Use more specific cards (parrotfish, angelfish, etc.) when identifiable.

taxa.description: Small crustaceans including cleaners and powerful mantis shrimp.
taxa.id_tips: Cleaner shrimp in anemones/crevices; mantis shrimp in burrows with stalked eyes.

taxa.description: Powerful stomatopods with extraordinary vision; smashers and spearers.
taxa.id_tips: Peacock mantis: rainbow carapace at burrow entrance. Don't poke.
taxa.danger_notes: Can strike hard — keep fingers clear of burrows.

taxa.description: Beak-mouthed herbivores that scrape algae and produce sand.
taxa.id_tips: Fused beak teeth, bright colors, often scraping coral rock; night mucus cocoons.

taxa.description: Flower-like cnidarians that host clownfish and cleaner shrimp.
taxa.id_tips: Tentacle tips and column color separate species; look for resident fish.

taxa.description: Laterally compressed reef fish with a distinctive cheek spine.
taxa.id_tips: Look for the preopercular spine; juveniles often differently patterned.

taxa.description: Oval reef fish with a locking dorsal trigger spine; some nest aggressively.
taxa.id_tips: Small mouth, diamond body; titan triggerfish: yellow-green with dark blotches.
taxa.danger_notes: Nesting titans can charge — give wide berth in season.

taxa.description: Small colorful disk-shaped reef fish, often in pairs.
taxa.id_tips: Pointed snout, bold patterns; false eye spots common.

taxa.description: Schooling reef predators, often under ledges and wrecks by day.
taxa.id_tips: Sloping forehead, prominent canine teeth; schools in mid-water at dusk.

taxa.description: Fast silver predators hunting along walls and blue water.
taxa.id_tips: Forked tail, streamlined body; GTs are thick and dark-finned.

taxa.description: Elongated relatives of seahorses; ghost pipefish are masters of camouflage.
taxa.id_tips: Scan crinoids and soft coral for matching pipe shapes; trumpetfish hover vertically.

taxa.description: Long thin ambush predators that hang vertically among gorgonians.
taxa.id_tips: Pencil-thin body, tiny mouth at end of tubular snout.

taxa.description: Common tropical reef shark resting in caves and under ledges by day.
taxa.id_tips: White tips on dorsal and caudal fins; slender body; often in pairs in caves.

taxa.description: Shallow-water reef shark with distinctive black fin tips.
taxa.id_tips: Black tips on all fins especially dorsal; often in lagoons and reef flats.

taxa.description: Sluggish bottom shark often resting under ledges in the Caribbean.
taxa.id_tips: Two barbels at mouth, tan color, dorsal fins far back.

taxa.description: Generic shark sighting when species not identified.
Largest fish; filter feeder often at plankton blooms and baitballs.
taxa.id_tips: Checkerboard white spots, flat head, enormous size — stay clear of the tail.

taxa.description: Pelagic shark with elongated upper caudal lobe used to stun prey.
taxa.id_tips: Absurdly long upper tail lobe; often at cleaning stations at dawn (e.g. Malapascua).

taxa.description: Spotted/banded bottom sharks resting on sand (taxonomy labels often mixed in field reports).
taxa.id_tips: Zebra/leopard (Stegostoma): ridges on body, long tail. Wobbegongs: ornate dermal lobes.

taxa.description: Iconic macro subjects clinging to seagrass, hydroid, and man-made debris.
taxa.id_tips: Scan carefully — cryptic. Males have brood pouch.

taxa.description: Cryptic ambush predators with a fishing lure (illicium).
taxa.id_tips: Scan sponges and rubble for mismatched texture; lure above the mouth.

taxa.description: Anemone-associated damselfish; species vary by stripe pattern and host.
taxa.id_tips: Always with anemone; count stripes and note color for species.

taxa.description: Echinoderms on reef and sand; crown-of-thorns is a coral predator.
taxa.id_tips: COTS: many spines, 10–20 arms. Blue Linckia common on Indo-Pacific reefs.

taxa.description: Spiny echinoderms in crevices and on reef flats.
taxa.id_tips: Long black Diadema spines common; avoid contact.

taxa.description: Slow reef fish with armor (box) or inflate (puffer); some toxic.
taxa.id_tips: Boxfish: rigid cubic body. Puffers: inflate when threatened.
taxa.danger_notes: Some tissues toxic if eaten; don't harass.

taxa.description: Fast pelagic predators occasionally seen off walls and seamounts.
taxa.id_tips: Crescent tail, metallic flanks, high cruising speed.

taxa.description: Color-changing cephalopods; giant cuttlefish aggregate to breed in South Australia.
taxa.id_tips: W-shaped pupil, undulating fin skirt, cuttlebone internally.

taxa.description: Schooling cephalopods often seen at night or over sand.
taxa.id_tips: Torpedo body, triangular fins, color flashes; reef squid hover in groups.

taxa.description: Colonies of eels protruding from sand patches like a garden.
taxa.id_tips: Approach slowly — they withdraw into burrows when startled.

taxa.description: Huge Indo-Pacific wrasse with a bulbous forehead; threatened.
taxa.id_tips: Massive lips, hump on forehead of adults, green maze pattern.

taxa.description: Diverse colorful reef fish including cleaners and Napoleon.
taxa.id_tips: Protrusible jaws, continuous dorsal fin; many change sex/color with age.

taxa.description: Thick-lipped reef fish; juveniles often spotted and dance oddly.
taxa.id_tips: Juveniles: high contrast spots, exaggerated swimming. Adults school under ledges.

taxa.description: Oval herbivores with a scalpel-like spine on the caudal peduncle.
taxa.id_tips: Look for the spine spot near the tail; schools graze algae.

taxa.description: Tall-bodied curious fish that often approach divers on wrecks.
taxa.id_tips: Very tall compressed body; juveniles may have long fins.

taxa.description: Giant oceanic fish often at cleaning stations in cold upwellings (e.g. Bali).
taxa.id_tips: Huge truncated body, tall dorsal/anal fins; usually near thermocline.

taxa.description: Marine mammals occasionally encountered on blue-water or channel dives.
taxa.id_tips: Horizontal tail beat (vs fish), social groups, acoustic clicks.

taxa.description: Drifting cnidarians; blooms can be seasonal hazards or attractions (e.g. stingless lakes).
taxa.id_tips: Bell + tentacles; give stinging species space.
taxa.danger_notes: Many species sting — know local hazards (box jelly, Portuguese man o' war).

taxa.description: Sausage-shaped echinoderms on sand and reef; important detritivores.
taxa.id_tips: Slow crawlers on sand; some expel sticky tubules when threatened.

taxa.description: Barbel-equipped sand foragers often in small groups.
taxa.id_tips: Two chin barbels actively probing sand.

taxa.description: Large temperate/tropical eels in wrecks and rocky holes.
taxa.id_tips: Grey/brown, no patterned spots like many morays; common in European wrecks.

taxa.description: Venomous marine snakes of the Indo-Pacific; generally not aggressive.
taxa.id_tips: Paddle-like tail, nostrils on top of snout.

taxa.description: Seasonal migratory whale; singers and calves in warm-water breeding grounds.
taxa.id_tips: Long pectoral fins, knobbly head, bushy blow; seasonal only.

taxa.description: Apex marine mammal; rare but iconic at some cold-water and polar sites.
taxa.id_tips: Tall dorsal fin (male), black/white pattern, pod structure.

taxa.description: Schooling baitfish forming seasonal baitballs pursued by predators.
taxa.id_tips: Dense silver schools; watch for predators and birds above.

taxa.description: Small territorial reef fish including chromis clouds over coral heads.
taxa.id_tips: Often defend nest algae patches aggressively.

taxa.description: Large bivalves embedded in reef; colorful mantle.
taxa.id_tips: Iridescent mantle spots; shell embedded in coral rock.

taxa.description: Generic open-water fish assemblage (jacks, tuna, sharks, etc.).
Burrow-dwelling fish that hover above holes; males mouth-brood eggs.
taxa.id_tips: Large jaw, hovering over a sand burrow entrance.

taxa.description: Camouflaged flatfish on sand; both eyes on one side.
taxa.id_tips: Scan sand for eye bumps and outline that doesn't match ripples.

taxa.description: Ray with a shark-like body resting on sand.
taxa.id_tips: Pointed snout, ray-like pectoral disc fused to body.

taxa.description: Largest turtle; leathery ridged carapace; mostly pelagic.
taxa.id_tips: No hard scutes — ridges on a dark rubbery shell.

taxa.description: Sharks with a distinctive hammer-shaped cephalofoil; often at seamounts and cleaning stations.
taxa.id_tips: Wide flattened head, tall dorsal fin; often in schools at dawn.

taxa.description: Large-headed hard-shelled sea turtle common on temperate and subtropical reefs.
taxa.id_tips: Very large head, heart-shaped carapace, reddish-brown color.

taxa.description: Playful pinnipeds at temperate Pacific and Southern Ocean sites.
taxa.id_tips: External ear flaps, rear flippers can walk on land; curious underwater.

taxa.description: Small Indo-Pacific stingray with electric blue spots on sand and in caves.
taxa.id_tips: Oval disc with vivid blue spots and blue-edged tail stripes.

taxa.description: Schooling mid-water reef fish, often yellow/blue streaming along walls.
taxa.id_tips: Forked tail, streamlined; schools in open water near reef edges.

taxa.description: Long-legged crabs, often decorated with sponges and algae.
taxa.id_tips: Spindly legs; check soft coral and wrecks at night.

taxa.description: Huge vase-shaped sponges that structure Caribbean and Indo-Pacific reefs.
taxa.id_tips: Barrel or vase shape large enough to swim beside (don't touch).

taxa.description: Temperate and tropical bass-like fishes often on wrecks and rocky reefs.
taxa.id_tips: Heavy body, large mouth; species vary widely by region.

taxa.description: Laterally compressed temperate reef/coastal fish common in Europe and elsewhere.
taxa.id_tips: Deep body, forked tail; often in small groups over rock.

taxa.description: Common Indo-Pacific reef shark patrolling passes and walls.
taxa.id_tips: Uniform grey, black trailing edge on caudal fin; often mid-water.

taxa.description: Fast schooling pelagic fish with wavy flank markings.
taxa.id_tips: Streamlined, spotted or barred flanks, high speed along reef edges.

taxa.description: Often a PADI mislabel for barracuda or temperate pike in lakes/quarries.
taxa.id_tips: Long snout and teeth; confirm local species — may be barracuda on reefs.

taxa.description: Temperate freshwater/brackish fish seen on quarry and lake dives.
taxa.id_tips: Vertical bars, spiny dorsal fin; freshwater sites.

taxa.description: Large freshwater fish common in European quarry and lake dives.
taxa.id_tips: Barbels at mouth, large scales, bronze color.

taxa.description: Carpet sharks common on Indo-Pacific reefs and under ledges in Raja Ampat/Misool.
taxa.id_tips: Flattened ornate head with dermal lobes; rests on sand and under overhangs.

taxa.description: Tiny seahorses on gorgonian sea fans — classic Misool / Raja Ampat macro.
taxa.id_tips: Scan Muricella sea fans carefully; match color to the fan.

taxa.description: Larger of the two manta species; visits Misool Magic Mountain with reef mantas.
taxa.id_tips: Larger disc, black/white ventral morphs, dorsal spot pattern differs from reef manta.
